To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the oscillation period in a metallic ring is hc/e, (2) the supercurrent is periodic in flux with period hc/2, but (3) the periodicity of the total current in a ring is not necessarily hc/2e.
the period of the supercurrent in a loop is hc/e in the normal state, hc/2e for weak superconductivity, and hc/4e for strong superconductivity.

in a superconducting loop with a large enough ring radius R and with a sufficiently strong magnetic field B, the oscillation period can be close to hc/e and that in a superconductor with a small R, or in a weak field, the current can exhibit a periodicity close to hc/2 e.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between superconductivity and the quantum Hall effect.
a fundamental question of the quantum theory of metals and superconductors: how the quantum oscillation period of a current in a ring is related to the electron interactions.

the following two questions: (i) What is the periodicity of the current in a ring when the electron interactions are weak, i.e. in the normal state of a metal? (ii) What is the crossover from the periodic normal current to periodic supercurrent in a ring when a pairing interaction is turned on?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the period is hc/2e for a superconducting loop with an odd number of electrons and hc/e for a superconductivity loop with an even number of electrons.
the period of oscillations of the current in superconducting loops is hc/2e, while in normal metallic loops it is hc/e.
the periodicity of the current in a ring depends on the electron interactions and on the ring geometry, and is determined by the ratio of the electron interaction energy to the charging energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the periodicity crossover is a very delicate effect, and it is not necessarily true that the period of the oscillating supercurrent is always half of the period of the normal current in the ring.
the supercurrent in a superconducting loop is always periodic with the period hc/2 e, but the periodicity of the normal current in a metallic ring depends on the electron interactions.
the periodicity crossover is not always a clear indication of the onset of superconductivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the periodicity crossover from hc/e to hc/2 e in the supercurrent can be observed in the normal metal ring with an appropriate pairing interaction, which can be realized by a gate voltage in the two-dimensional electron gas.
the crossover from the normal to superconducting state in a loop is not necessarily accompanied by a change of the current oscillation period from hc/e to hc/2 e.
the periodicity of a supercurrent is not necessarily half that of the normal current, and that the crossover is not necessarily abrupt.
